question: Should historical `update --ref <tag-or-commit>` remain backward compatible as an implicit explicit restore, or should this release intentionally require callers to add `--restore`?
rationale: The new flag makes destructive replacement clearer, but rejecting an already documented command form breaks scripts and requires an explicit compatibility-policy decision.

options.title: Preserve `--ref` compatibility
options.body: Treat a non-empty historical ref as an explicit restore, while retaining `--restore` for latest-snapshot replacement.

options.title: Approve the CLI break
options.body: Require `--restore` with every historical ref and publish a deliberate upgrade notice for existing automation.

recommendation.title: Preserve `--ref` compatibility
recommendation.body: Treat a non-empty historical ref as an explicit restore, while retaining `--restore` for latest-snapshot replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: The submitted change defines the affected CLI and archive semantics; a broader history owner could not be established from the read-only inspection environment.
